messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated 5xx and gateway timeout rate detected for private VPC traffic to inference-gateway in eu-west-1. 5xx spike started ~1765123200, affecting ~3 private customers behind our transit firewall appliance. Severity: P1. Please ack.

oncall-ryan: ACK. I'm on it — scooping logs now. Which customers are impacted?

marie-sre: I'm seeing a surge of 502/504 from the gateway proxy logs:
```
2026-04-04T12:40:12Z gateway ERROR upstream_write_timeout: upstream response timed out after 10s, client=10.12.45.72
2026-04-04T12:40:13Z gateway ERROR 502 Bad Gateway from 172.31.22.8:443
2026-04-04T12:40:18Z gateway ERROR 504 Gateway Timeout to client 10.12.45.72
```

alice-netops: correlating with transit-fw logs — we're seeing a lot of connection tracking evictions and heavy SYN_RECV states on the stateful appliance. conntrack state snapshots: `conntrack -S` shows table nearing 95% used. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion + asymmetric path making NAT entries invalid.

oncall-ryan: Good catch. Any recent config pushes to the transit firewall or iptables rules?

alice-netops: We rolled a policy tweak at 12:20 — adding a DPI rule to block large UDP flows for one customer; shouldn't affect TCP but the appliance CPU spiked after the deploy. I'm pulling the deploy id.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-04-04T12:18:57 - transit-fw: policy/dpi-update - SUCCESS rollout to tranche-1 (66%)

jonah-support: Customer A reported timeouts from their routed private cluster to inference endpoints around 12:30. They see repeated TLS session resets.

marie-sre: Running tcpdump on gateway -> seeing lots of retransmits and RSTs to upstream inference hosts when flows return via transit-fw. There are asymmetric source IPs on the upstream side. Looks like SNAT mapping not stable.

alice-netops: Getting conntrack table dump (snippet):
```
# conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
198342
# conntrack -S | grep entries
entries 210000
allocated 199548
```
We have configured 200k as the conntrack limit but actual usage is near that. Evictions starting.

oncall-ryan: If conntrack is evicting established states, upstream responses can be dropped and the gateway will return 502/504. What's causing the large # of ephemeral sessions?

alice-netops: We're seeing a pattern: customers with high short-lived parallel connections (model inference clients with many concurrent short requests). The transit appliance is also doing TLS termination and session inspection; CPU and memory spike = slower conntrack reclaim.

marie-sre: Immediate mitigation options: 1) bypass transit appliance for affected routes (route via nat-gw pool), 2) increase conntrack table + ephemeral port range temporarily, 3) roll back DPI policy deploy. Recommend plan: roll back DPI policy, add temporary SNAT pool, and open ticket to temporarily enlarge conntrack.

oncall-ryan: Execute rollback and SNAT pool change now. Alice, can you apply? Marie, prepare a quick validation and health-check. Jonah, notify customers that we're mitigating (no public status yet until we confirm).

alice-netops: Rolling back transit-fw DPI policy now. Command: `fwctl rollback policy-id 2026-04-04-12:18`

alice-netops: Rollback accepted. appliance state: policy_active=policy-2026-03-29. CPU dropping from 94% -> 52% over 30s. Conntrack pressure easing.

alice-netops: Adding temporary SNAT pool and expanding ephemeral ports:
```
# iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.12.0.0/16 -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 54.23.11.200-54.23.11.210
# sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=350000
# sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
```

marie-sre: After SNAT pool applied, gateway logs show 200 responses resuming to most customers. 5xx rate dropped from 8% to 0.6% in 2 minutes. Running synthetic checks now (curl + repeated small requests).

jonah-support: Notifying affected customers A/B with an initial note: "We've detected transient timeouts to inference endpoints and are applying mitigations; you may see improved connectivity in the next few minutes. Support team will follow up with details."

tina-customer-ops: Please make sure we capture affected request ids for SLA credit assessment. I'll open a ticket and collect example traces.

marie-sre: Validation snippet: `for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://gateway.private.internal/v1/predict; done` -> 200 x49, 500 x1 (retries caught). Good.

alice-netops: conntrack usage post-mitigation: allocated 120k / entries 210k (note: entries count is configured ceiling); active states stable now. We should keep the SNAT pool and conntrack increase for 1 hour while we monitor.

oncall-ryan: Agreed. Monitor for 30 minutes then converge on long-term fix. Any sign of packet drops on the host NICs or kernel logs?

marie-sre: dmesg shows some conntrack eviction warnings earlier, none after rollback. NIC errors=0. TCP retransmit rate normalized.

alice-netops: We'll also schedule a transit-fw capacity bump (upgrade appliance or split traffic) and change DPI rollout gating so CPU-heavy rules are rolled to a canary tenant first.

jonah-support: Customer A acknowledges improved connectivity and will run load tests. Customer B still seeing intermittent 504s but reduced.

tina-customer-ops: I'll coordinate post-incident comms and SLA note draft. Please paste any request ids from gateways into the ticket.

marie-sre: Kicking off incident doc: short summary, timeline, customer impact (A,B,C), mitigations, and action items for next 72h.

oncall-ryan: Handoff: I'm going to hand to netops oncall after 40 minutes of clean metrics. If error rate stays <0.5% for 30m, we'll downgrade to P2 and schedule a postmortem. For now keeping P1 until confirmed.

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handover scheduled at 1765123656 from oncall-ryan -> alice-netops.

alice-netops: I'll take the handoff. Monitoring dashboards and will escalate if anything regresses.

marie-sre: Action items: (1) Formal postmortem with root cause: transit DPI policy CPU + conntrack pressure + insufficient SNAT pool; (2) Add automatic alert: conntrack_used_pct > 80% for transit-fw; (3) Limit concurrent short-lived connections per tenant and recommend client-side connection pooling docs; (4) Add canary gating for DPI policies.

jonah-support: Also add a runbook entry for 'transit-fw conntrack surge' with quick mitigations.

oncall-ryan: Final note while handing off: if you need me pinged, @ryan will be available for escalation. Good job team.

alice-netops: Acknowledged — taking over monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> monitoring. P1 -> P1 (monitoring). Updates will be logged to the incident ticket."
